title: The enthalpy of formation of ethanol from combustion data

stimulus.title: Three combustion reactions
stimulus.text: Carbon, hydrogen and ethanol each burn cleanly in oxygen, so their enthalpies of combustion can be measured.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The target reaction is 2 C(graphite) + 3 H₂(g) + ½ O₂(g) → C₂H₅OH(l). Identify which of the three reactions must be reversed to obtain the target, and explain why.

rubric.point: Reaction 3, because ethanol is a reactant in Reaction 3 but a product in the target
accept: reverse reaction 3 so that C₂H₅OH is on the product side

parts.sample: Reaction 3 must be reversed. In the target, ethanol is a product, but in Reaction 3 it is a reactant.

parts.label: b

rubric.point: Correct manipulation: Reaction 1 × 2, Reaction 2 × 3, Reaction 3 reversed, with each ΔH adjusted the same way

parts.sample: 2 × Reaction 1: 2 C + 2 O₂ → 2 CO₂, ΔH = −787.0 kJ. 3 × Reaction 2: 3 H₂ + 3/2 O₂ → 3 H₂O, ΔH = −857.4 kJ. Reaction 3 reversed: 2 CO₂ + 3 H₂O → C₂H₅OH + 3 O₂, ΔH = +1366.7 kJ. Adding, 2 CO₂, 3 H₂O and 3 O₂ cancel (leaving ½ O₂ on the left): ΔH° = −787.0 − 857.4 + 1366.7 = −277.7 kJ/mol.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The target reaction cannot be carried out in a lab, yet its ΔH° can be found from Reactions 1-3. Justify why this method gives the correct value.

rubric.point: Enthalpy is a state function, so ΔH depends only on the initial and final states; any set of steps that adds to the target has the same total ΔH
accept: Hess's law: ΔH does not depend on the path
the route does not matter because enthalpy is a state function

parts.sample: Enthalpy is a state function: ΔH depends only on the starting substances and the final substances, not on the route between them. Reactions 1-3, adjusted, add up to exactly the target, so their ΔH values add up to its ΔH.
